evidence: Loss of function: the mutant is cleaved and secreted normally but degrades the LDL receptor less well -- cells show +16% surface LDLR and +35% internalised LDL. Carriers have lower total and LDL cholesterol (LDL-C SMD -0.44).
source: Cameron et al. 2006 (via review PMC2952575); meta-analysis lipidworld 10.1186/s12944-017-0506-6

evidence: Defines the APOE epsilon4 isoform with rs7412. UK Biobank (n~379k): epsilon4 carriers have higher total and LDL cholesterol than epsilon3epsilon3.
Defines the APOE epsilon2 isoform with rs429358. UK Biobank (n~379k): epsilon2epsilon2 mean total cholesterol ~0.78 SD below epsilon3epsilon3; epsilon2epsilon3 also lower.

Reduced protein stability and reduced hepatic TM6SF2 protein. Overexpressing E167K in oleic-acid-treated Huh-7 cells raises lipid-droplet area; Tm6sf2 knockout mice and hepatocyte suppression recapitulate the carrier phenotype. Carriers have lower total cholesterol.

A knock-in mouse reproduces several traits of the locus including raised blood cholesterol and lower blood glucose; in human liver organoids the variant GKRP binds GCK less well and suppresses GCK activity less. Primarily a triglyceride/glucose variant.

Creates a C/EBP transcription-factor binding site and alters SORT1 expression in human-derived hepatocytes; siRNA knockdown and viral overexpression of Sort1 in mouse liver move plasma LDL-C via hepatic VLDL secretion. A later study perturbed the variant itself by CRISPR-Cas9 in primary human hepatocytes from heterozygous donors (SORT1 expression fell) and built a locus-humanised BAC mouse. CAVEAT: that study states rs12740374 tags the minor haplotype and any SNP on it could be causal, and the liver eQTL replicated poorly.
source: Musunuru et al. 2010 Nature (PMC3062476); follow-up PMC5746470

evidence: The minor allele raises LDLR expression in Huh7 luciferase reporters and EMSA places serum response element at the site. CAVEAT: in COMPLETE linkage disequilibrium with rs141787760, rs60173709 and rs57217136, and the same study finds rs57217136 equally functional (RAR and STAT1 binding). Not statistically identifiable from association data -- no method can single it out, and spreading PIP across the haplotype is the correct answer.
